Ben —

Thanks for the clear ask. Summary up front: Redwood supports two connectivity patterns for private traffic to customer resources:

1) VPC Peering (customer-managed): We create a peering attachment between Redwood-managed VPCs and your customer VPC. Traffic is routed over the peering connection; TLS terminates at the application layer inside the customer environment (customer TLS certs). No public egress IPs are required for peering.

2) Private Connect / Private Endpoint (customer-hosted endpoint): We provide an endpoint in a customer-assigned subnet (PrivateLink-style) that appears in the customer VPC. In this mode, traffic egresses from Redwood infrastructure but is routed into your private subnet via the endpoint; we document the endpoint behavior and expected IP ranges.

Attachments included: sig-responses-v2.pdf (answers & short configs), nimbus-vpc-diagram.png (annotated diagram for both flow types), peering-routes.txt (example route-table export).

Short answers to your bullets:
- Termination: For Private Connect, the endpoint is an ENI in the customer VPC (customer-managed) — so termination is inside the customer VPC. For VPC Peering, traffic is routed to your VPC over the peering attachment and terminates in your services.
- Egress IPs: We provide a small set of static egress IP prefixes for customer-facing outbound connections when Private Connect is used; when VPC peering is used, egress is not required for peer-to-peer internal traffic. See the section "Egress & NAT" in sig-responses-v2.pdf for CIDR blocks (we list both stable ranges and the maintenance notification policy).
- Route/peering evidence: peering-routes.txt contains an example export (route IDs redacted) as requested. If you need console screenshots, we can take them as soon as you confirm which account/attachment ID you want evidence for.

I'll let Karthik give the more detailed ops steps and an exact traceroute sample.

—Rishi
Director, Partner Security Ops
Redwood Inference
